ad.title: Active Directory (domain users, Domain Admins sign in)

backup.title: Backup (restic to the backup disk, restore drills)

docker.title: Docker host with a web page to manage it

steps.title: Manager
steps.text: You can change it later. The apps and their data stay when you switch.
steps.question: Which page should manage Docker?

options.label: The web interface of hobnix
options.text: State, start, stop, logs and pull of every app. Built later: for now the choice is recorded.

options.label: Arcane
options.text: A page of its own that also edits compose files.

options.label: Portainer
options.text: The most features, and the most memory.

options.label: None
options.text: Docker only. You manage it with the command line.

steps.title: Size
steps.text: It can be resized later with hs ct docker set.
steps.question: How large should the Docker container be?

options.label: Small
options.text: 2 GB memory, 2 CPUs

options.label: Medium
options.text: 4 GB memory, 4 CPUs

options.label: Large
options.text: 8 GB memory, 8 CPUs

docs.title: Documentation in the web interface (guides and command reference)

edge-ports.title: Edge node: public game and call ports

edge-watcher.title: Edge node: outside watcher of the home server

gateway.title: Gateway proxy (Traefik: local names for the services)

steps.title: How connections arrive
steps.text: A Cloudflare tunnel needs no open port. A router port forward opens 443 and 80 of this server to the internet.
steps.question: How should connections from the internet reach this server?

options.label: Cloudflare tunnel
options.text: No open port on the router. Traefik takes the tunnel on port 8081.

options.label: Router port forward
options.text: The router forwards ports 443 and 80 to this server.

steps.title: Public domains
steps.text: The names the internet uses to reach this server. The local domain and its wildcard record come from the Active Directory and are shown in the status above.
steps.question: Which public domains should reach this server?

steps.title: Certificates
steps.text: Let's Encrypt certificates are requested either over HTTPS (TLS-ALPN-01, the default, port 443 must reach this server) or through Cloudflare DNS-01 (the API token is a credential, never a command argument). Use the staging service while you test.
steps.question: How should certificates be requested?

options.label: Cloudflare DNS-01
options.text: No open port needed. The API token is set with hs gateway acme-token.

steps.title: Login
steps.text: The login is set per service, not for the whole gateway: open a service under Instances, Services and choose its login there.
steps.question: Where is the login set?

steps.title: Unknown names
steps.text: What a request for a name this server does not know gets as an answer, for the local and for the public side.
steps.question: What should a request for an unknown name get?

live-state.title: Live state (Redis cache for the web interface)

storage.title: Storage (ZFS or SnapRAID pools, shares, encrypted disks)

testlab.title: Test-lab (builds the installer ISO and runs it in a nested VM)

steps.title: New shares
steps.text: Shares that are in the backup now stay in it, whatever you choose.
steps.question: Should a new share be backed up by itself?

options.label: No, I switch each share on
options.text: Big, replaceable data such as media does not fill the backup disk.

options.label: Yes, every new share is backed up
options.text: Nothing new is forgotten. The backup disk fills faster.

steps.title: New containers
steps.text: Containers that are in the backup now stay in it, whatever you choose.
steps.question: Should a container that an app sets up be backed up by itself?

options.label: Yes, every new container is backed up
options.text: The app and its data are safe from the first day.

options.label: No, I switch each container on
options.text: Only the containers you pick go into the backup.

steps.title: Local names
steps.text: The label in front of your domain for this server's names, such as jellyfin.home.example.com. Empty means the server's name.

steps.title: Who may use the shares
steps.text: The networks whose PCs may open the Samba shares, separated by spaces. Keep 127.0.0.1.

steps.title: Addresses the router hands out
steps.text: The last number of the first and the last address your router gives out by DHCP, such as 100 199. Only used to point out containers without a fixed address.

steps.title: Incus web UI
steps.text: The Incus web UI and the network address of the Incus API.
steps.question: Should the Incus web UI and remote access stay open?

options.label: Keep it open
options.text: https://<server>:8443/ui/ works and incus remote add can reach the server.

options.label: Close it
options.text: Port 8443 closes; Incus is reachable only on this machine.

steps.title: Network card
steps.text: The port the server's cable is in. Everything goes through it: containers, shares, Tailscale. A wrong card leaves the server offline after the rebuild; the plan asks you to type the card's name.
steps.question: Which network card is the cable in?

steps.title: Parity updates
steps.text: New and changed files are unprotected until the next run, and each run wakes every disk.
steps.question: How often should the SnapRAID parity be updated?

options.label: Once a night
options.text: At 03:00, so the disks can sleep the rest of the day.

options.label: Every 12 hours
options.text: Changes are protected sooner; the disks wake twice a day.

options.label: Every 4 hours
options.text: Smallest window without protection; the disks wake six times a day.

steps.title: Snapshots
steps.text: Hourly ZFS snapshots: the last 24 hours, 7 days and 4 weeks are kept. They hold deleted files, so they use space.
steps.question: Should every share get automatic snapshots?

options.label: No snapshots
options.text: No extra space is used; a deleted file is gone.

options.label: Hourly snapshots
options.text: You can get an older version of a file back.

steps.title: Disk sleep
steps.text: Spinning bulk, parity and backup disks only. The first access after a sleep takes 10 to 20 seconds.
steps.question: Should the data disks go to sleep when idle?

options.label: Never
options.text: The disks stay ready; no waiting.

options.label: After 20 minutes
options.text: Saves power and noise on a server that is idle at times.

options.label: After 60 minutes
options.text: Saves power while short pauses do not wake-sleep the disks.

steps.title: Browser terminal
steps.text: A Terminal button in the top bar and on each instance. A change takes effect at once.
steps.question: Should the web interface offer a terminal?

options.label: No
options.text: Shell access stays with ssh.

options.label: Yes
options.text: Everyone who can sign in to the web interface gets a shell as adminuser.

steps.title: Idle time
steps.text: Only typing counts, not output.
steps.question: When should an idle terminal window close?

options.label: After 30 minutes without typing
options.text: The shell keeps running; signing in again reattaches it.

options.label: After 10 minutes without typing
options.text: The shell keeps running; signing in again reattaches it.

options.label: After 60 minutes without typing
options.text: The shell keeps running; signing in again reattaches it.

steps.title: Longest connection
steps.text: After that the window closes and can be opened again.
steps.question: How long may one terminal connection last?

options.label: 8 hours
options.text: Then it closes and reattaches the same way.

options.label: 2 hours
options.text: Then it closes and reattaches the same way.

options.label: 12 hours
options.text: The web login itself ends after 12 hours.

steps.title: Language
steps.text: Commands, options and file names stay English.
steps.question: Which language should hs and the web interface use?

options.label: English
options.text: Messages and descriptions are in English.

options.label: Deutsch
options.text: Messages and descriptions are in German.

steps.title: Time zone
steps.text: Such as Europe/Vienna. Empty means UTC. The logs, the timers and the times in the apps use it.

steps.title: Keyboard
steps.text: The keyboard layout of the console on the server itself, such as de. Empty means US.
